title: burst debt recovery and toolcall sanity layer for gateway streaming
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Gateway: introduce burst-debt recovery to smooth short-lived high ingress bursts; tighten toolcall handshake sanity checks and add a compatibility fallback for legacy OpenAI-style fncall sequences. No customer-facing API changes; rollout controlled by feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Customers observed transient 503/stream resets when large numbers of small streaming requests arrive in short bursts (spiky PLG traffic). Root cause is short-term headroom exhaustion in route credit accounting combined with lingering per-connection write buffers that block proxy writers and prevent fast recovery. This PR introduces a conservative "burst debt recovery" mechanism plus a lightweight toolcall sanity layer to reduce malformed fncall handshake aborts and provide a compatibility fallback for older OpenAI-style tool call sequences.

What this changes (high level):
- Route credit recovery: after a short burst that temporarily drives a route into negative credit, we now allow controlled recovery credits that replenish at a higher rate for the first N seconds to avoid extended quarantine. Recovery parameters are tunable per-route.
- Transient buffer trimming: proxy writer now enforces a soft egress queue TTL that will drop/aggregate stale fragments older than configured window to prevent write stalls from building up under bursty ingress.
- Toolcall sanity layer: added strict pre-flight validation for structured fncall payloads, with fast-fail and normalized handshake for older OpenAI-compatible payload shapes. This reduces stateful retry thrashing between gateway and backend runtimes.
- Compatibility fallback: when a legacy OpenAI-style fncall pattern is detected, gateway temporarily routes to the compat shim which performs normalization and preserves streaming envelopes. This path is rate-limited and opt-in via feature flag to avoid unexpected perf regressions.
- Observability and metrics: new metrics for burst debt events, recovery credits granted, trimmed fragments, and compat fallback invocations; added alert tuning suggestions in docs.

Why this is different from prior efforts: Previous fixes adjusted static backpressure thresholds and increased global headroom which reduced some failures but caused higher mean latency and cost. The approach here focuses on quick, targeted recovery and shaping of transient queues rather than increasing static capacity. It also addresses fncall handshake instability separately so we don't mix control-plane and protocol fixes.

Checklist: 
- [x] unit tests for credit recovery state machine
- [x] e2e replay of PLG burst trace (integration_tests/streaming_e2e.py)
- [x] added metrics and dashboards (prometheus labels + grafana panels)

Commits summary:
- 1a2b3c4: gateway: implement burst debt recovery state machine and per-route policy (core logic + tests)
- 5d6e7f8: proxy: add soft egress queue TTL and fragment trimming; add metric plumbing
- 9a0b1c2: openai_compat: lightweight normalization shim and detection heuristics
- 3d4e5f6: docs: add guidance and dashboard snippets for tuning recovery parameters

Files changed (high level):
- gateway/credit/recovery_state.go -> implements fast-recovery logic and policy config
- gateway/routing/rule_engine.go -> integrates recovery tokens into route admission
- gateway/proxy/egress_writer.go -> soft TTL trimming, aggregation hooks, added metrics
- gateway/config/profiles.yaml -> default recovery policy and TTL profiles
- openai_compat/compat_shim.go -> detection + normalization + streaming envelope passthrough (opt-in)
- docs/gateway/burst-recovery.md -> operator guide and suggested SLO adjustments
- integration_tests/streaming_e2e.py -> reproducer and regression assertion

Testing and CI: All unit/integration tests pass on CI (full matrix). Load replay locally and in bench-lab shows 3-10x reduction in multi-second route quarantines during burst traces while median latency unchanged. Compatibility shim path adds ~1-2% CPU when enabled under heavy fncall volume; flagged in release notes so customers can opt in.

Review thread highlights:
- Liam: "Can you clarify the conditions where we grant fast recovery credits? We should avoid starving other routes."
- Maya: "Recovery credits are per-route and capped by a windowed aggregate; the algorithm only applies if route util is > 90% and global spare GPU headroom is < 5%. Added tests to validate no global starvation."
- Sara: "Need an integration test that asserts the compat shim does not alter event ordering for streaming fncalls."
- Maya: "Added e2e that asserts ordering and idempotency for the shim path; included a defensive checksum header we verify in the test."
- Tobias: "Consider making the TTL trimming configurable by route weight — low-criticality routes can be more aggressive."
- Maya: "Exposed TTL profile in profiles.yaml with sensible defaults; documented operator tuning guidance."

Post-merge notes: Feature is behind feature flag and will be rolled out graded by region. We'll monitor new metrics (burst_debt_events, recovery_credits, trimmed_fragments, compat_fallbacks) and watch for increased 429/410 patterns inadvertently caused by trimming. Ops runbook updated with rollback steps (toggle feature flag, revert policy to conservative profile).
